## Keras Examples {#sec-keras-examples}

**maidr** draws the training curves of a Keras model. Pass what `model.fit`
returns to `maidr.keras.plot_history()`, and hand the figure to `maidr.show()`,
`maidr.render()` or `maidr.save_html()`: each metric can then be read from the
keyboard, as sound, as text and in braille. To follow a model while it trains,
pass `maidr.keras.MaidrCallback` to `model.fit`. For the curves TensorBoard
logs, see the [TensorBoard](examples-tensorboard.qmd) page.

::: {.callout-warning title="Experimental"}
Keras support is **experimental**. What it draws, and how, may change without a
deprecation period: see [Plot Type Stability](stability.qmd#keras-support).
:::

`import maidr` does not load Keras: import `maidr.keras` when you use it.
`plot_history()` also reads the plain `history.history` dictionary, so it works
on a history saved to disk, with no Keras installed.

### Training Curves from model.fit

One chart per metric, the loss first, each with a *training* and a
*validation* line along the epochs, counted from 1 as Keras counts them. The
left and right arrow keys move along the epochs, up and down move to the other
line, and Page Up and Page Down move between the charts. A metric logged
without a validation value, such as the learning rate, is one line named for
itself.

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Two line charts, the loss and the accuracy at each epoch, each with a training and a validation line
import maidr
from maidr.keras import plot_history

# What `history = model.fit(..., validation_split=0.2)` holds in
# `history.history`; pass `history` itself just the same.
history = {
    "loss": [0.69, 0.52, 0.41, 0.35, 0.31, 0.29, 0.27, 0.26],
    "accuracy": [0.55, 0.74, 0.82, 0.86, 0.88, 0.89, 0.90, 0.91],
    "val_loss": [0.62, 0.47, 0.40, 0.37, 0.36, 0.36, 0.37, 0.39],
    "val_accuracy": [0.66, 0.79, 0.83, 0.85, 0.86, 0.86, 0.85, 0.85],
}
maidr.show(plot_history(history))
```

The validation loss stops falling after the fifth epoch and starts to rise
while the training loss keeps falling: the model has begun to overfit.
`metrics=` keeps only the metrics you name, in that order, such as
`plot_history(history, metrics=["loss"])`.

### Following a Model While It Trains

`MaidrCallback` writes an accessible page of the same charts every `every`
epochs, and a last time when training ends. Open the page while the model
trains and reload it to hear how far it has come; the page is replaced in one
step, so a reload never meets a half-written file. With no path, the charts
are shown in the notebook when training ends.

```python
from maidr.keras import MaidrCallback

model.fit(
    x, y,
    validation_split=0.2,
    epochs=50,
    callbacks=[MaidrCallback("training.html", every=5)],
)
```

The callback records the epoch of every value, so validation run only every
few epochs (`validation_freq=`) is placed on the epochs it was run on, which
`plot_history()` cannot tell from a `History`.
